entities.summary:
Warmund, also known as Garmond, Gormond, Germond, Guarmond, or Waremond, was the Latin Patriarch of Jerusalem from 1118 until his death at Sidon in 1128.

As the head of the Latin Church in the Holy Land, Warmund played a crucial role in the complex web of alliances and rivalries between the various Christian states and Muslim emirates of the region. His tenure was marked by a series of diplomatic efforts to maintain the fragile peace between the Crusader kingdoms and the Ayyubid dynasty.

Despite these efforts, Warmund's legacy is also marked by controversy, particularly with regard to his role in the persecution of Jewish communities in Jerusalem. His actions were widely condemned by the Jewish authorities, who saw him as a symbol of Christian intolerance and oppression.
